body_markdown:
If your hair snaps when you brush it, feels rough after color, or looks frayed from heat styling, it is easy to reach for anything labeled “strengthening.” The harder question is what kind of strengthening your hair is asking for: protein support, bond repair, or a routine that uses both with intention.


For weak, breakage-prone hair, bond repair is usually the stronger fit when the damage pattern points to color, bleach, heat styling, brushing, or repeated stress. Protein-based strengthening can help hair feel temporarily reinforced and more manageable, but bond repair is designed for damage within the hair’s structure. A shampoo can support the routine, but breakage-prone hair often needs more than one rinse-off step.


That is the lens we use here: match the product to the damage, keep expectations realistic, and build a routine that does the job without turning your shower into a science project.


## **Protein Strengthening vs Bond Repair: What Each Is Trying To Do**


Protein-based strengthening shampoos are often chosen when hair feels weak, limp, or over-soft. These formulas may use proteins, peptides, amino acids, or conditioning agents to help the hair feel stronger, smoother, or easier to style. Think of protein as support for the feel of the hair.


Bond repair is different. It is designed around the bonds within damaged hair structure. At OLAPLEX, our bond-building approach is rooted in patented technology, with products made to support repair at the level where damage can leave hair feeling fragile, rough, or prone to snapping. \[1\] \[2\]


The format matters, too. Shampoo is a rinse-off step. It can be a smart place to cleanse while supporting strength, hydration, shine, smoothness, and a better finished feel, but it should not carry the whole routine alone when hair is visibly damaged or breaking. That is where a treatment step can make the routine feel more targeted.


## **Choose By Damage Pattern, Not By Buzzword**


The best choice is not “protein is good” or “bond repair is good.” It is: what is your hair showing you?


**If your hair feels or looks like this** **Start here** **Why it fits** **Watch for**


Snaps easily after color, bleach, heat, brushing, or repeated styling


Bond repair


Designed for bond-related damage inside the hair structure


Do not expect one shampoo to do everything


Feels limp, overly soft, or hard to style


Protein-based strengthening may help


Can support the feel of stronger, more manageable hair


If hair starts to feel stiff, dry, or less flexible, reassess


Looks dull, rough, frizzy, or harder to detangle


Bond-maintenance shampoo plus conditioning care


Helps combine cleansing with a smoother, more conditioned finish


Keep treatment and conditioner steps in the routine when damage is more obvious


You want a simple maintenance wash for medium, thick, or coarse hair


Nº.4 Bond Maintenance Shampoo, Liter 1000mL


A highly concentrated strengthening shampoo for medium to coarse hair that gently cleanses while repairing everyday damage, reinforcing hair bonds, nourishing, hydrating, and boosting shine in one wash\[2\]


Use a dedicated treatment when repair is the main goal


A useful rule: if your hair’s weakness followed a service, hot tools, tight styling, repeated brushing stress, or a long stretch of “I know I should have been gentler,” reach for bond repair first. If your main goal is body, grip, or a stronger feel on otherwise manageable hair, protein may have a role.


## **Where Nº.4 Fits In A Breakage-Prone Routine**


Our Olaplex Nº.4 BOND MAINTENANCE™ STRENGTHENING SHAMPOO is the bond-maintenance shampoo example in this guide because it sits in the cleansing step you already use. It is made for medium, thick, and coarse hair textures, and the liter size gives you a 1000mL format for a routine you return to often.\[2\]


The benefit is not just that it cleanses. Nº.4 provides a reparative cleanse that strengthens, hydrates, and boosts shine with every wash.\[2\] It is formulated with a gentle blend of coconut oil-derived surfactants and gently cleanses without stripping essential moisture.\[2\] In use, that means your wash step can feel less like a reset button that leaves hair bare and more like the first move in a stronger, smoother finish.


For the visible finish, Nº.4 is clinically proven to boost shine, smooth, and reduce frizz.\[2\] It also boosts shine, smooths, and reduces frizz in one wash, and it is clinically proven to reduce split ends.\[2\] Keep that last point in the right lane: split-end claims are not a promise to permanently mend every frayed end. They are part of the supported performance picture for the product.


Nº.4 can be used for daily cleansing or as often as hair is washed.\[2\] Because the formula is highly concentrated, a little is designed to go a long way.\[2\] It also includes our OLAPLEX Signature Scent with Grapefruit Zest, Sugared Mint, Ginger, and Crushed Sage scent notes, which gives the wash step a bright, clean finish without making fragrance the main event.\[2\]


## **When To Add N°.3PLUS Before Shampoo**


If you are comparing protein and bond repair because your hair is actively breaking, a treatment step is often the more focused move. Our N°.3PLUS is a protein-free pre-shampoo treatment used in the shower before shampoo and conditioner.\[1\]


N°.3PLUS is a 3-minute pre-shampoo treatment. You apply it generously to wet hair from roots to ends, then rinse after 3 minutes before moving into shampoo and conditioner.\[1\] It is intended for use every 1–3 washes, and can be used daily if desired.\[1\]


This is where routine logic gets clearer:


-


Use N°.3PLUS when repair is the priority.


-


Use Nº.4 as the bond-maintenance cleansing step.


-


Keep conditioner in the routine when softness, slip, and detangling matter.


N°.3PLUS is formulated as a protein-free, color-safe hair treatment.\[1\] It uses patented OLAPLEX Bond Building Technology™ and a Damage Defense Cationic Complex, and it is designed to rebuild all three key hair bonds from cortex to cuticle.\[1\] It is clinically proven to create 3X softer hair and 3X stronger hair after 4 uses vs. bleached hair.\[1\]


If your hair has been through bleach, color, heat, or repeated styling stress, that treatment-before-shampoo format can be the difference between a routine that feels like maintenance and one that feels targeted.


## **What The System Claims Really Mean**


Here is the important part: system numbers belong to the system.


When Nº.3PLUS, Nº.4, and Nº.5 are used together as a system, the supported results include hair that is 90% smoother, better detangling, and more conditioned.\[2\] Those are not shampoo-only claims. They describe what is supported when the products are used together as that full system.


That distinction matters because it helps you choose without overloading one product with every job. Nº.4 is your bond-maintenance shampoo. N°.3PLUS is your dedicated pre-shampoo repair treatment. Nº.5 completes the named system in the supported system-performance claim, but this guide’s main decision is about choosing the right strengthening path: protein feel support, bond-repair care, or a routine that uses the right step at the right time.


## **A Simple Decision Path**


If your hair is weak or breakage-prone, use this as your quick read before you buy:


1.


Look at the cause.


If the weakness followed color, bleach, heat, brushing, or repeated styling, start with bond repair.


2.


Look at the feel.


If hair feels limp and hard to style but not visibly damaged, protein-based strengthening may help the feel.


3.


Look at the reaction.


If a protein-heavy routine leaves hair stiff, dry, or less flexible, shift away from that approach and reassess.


4.


Look at the format.


If you want daily or frequent cleansing support, choose a strengthening shampoo. If damage is the main concern, add a treatment step before shampoo.


5.


Look at the routine.


For the most supported OLAPLEX breakage, hydration, smoothness, detangling, and conditioning numbers, keep the full Nº.3PLUS, Nº.4, and Nº.5 system in mind rather than crediting one product alone.\[2\]


Strong hair is not about doing the most. It is about choosing the step that matches the damage.


## **How To Read Strengthening Claims Without Overthinking Them**


Product claims in this guide come from our official product information, including scientific research and professional use where stated. Broad hair-care decisions still need common sense: a shampoo is a wash step, a treatment is a treatment step, and a full system claim should stay tied to the full system.


That is why we do not frame protein and bond repair as enemies. They can both belong in the larger strengthening conversation. The smarter question is whether your hair needs temporary support for feel, or whether the pattern points to bond-related damage from color, heat, styling, or repeated stress.


If you want a bond-maintenance shampoo for frequent cleansing, Nº.4 is built for that role. If your hair needs a more focused repair step, add N°.3PLUS before shampoo. Then let the rest of your routine support softness, slip, and manageability so your hair feels as good as it looks.


## **FAQ**


### **Is Olaplex protein-free?**


N°.3PLUS is formulated as a protein-free, color-safe hair treatment.\[1\] In this guide, it is the protein-free bond-repair treatment example for hair that needs a focused pre-shampoo repair step.


### **Can a shampoo repair breakage on its own?**


A shampoo can support repair and maintenance, but it should not be treated as the entire breakage routine. Nº.4 provides a reparative cleanse that strengthens, hydrates, and boosts shine with every wash, and it is clinically proven to reduce split ends.\[2\] For supported system breakage results, the 49% reduction in breakage claim belongs to the full Nº.3PLUS, Nº.4, and Nº.5 system, not to shampoo alone.\[2\]


### **Can protein make breakage-prone hair feel worse?**


It can feel like the wrong fit if your hair starts to feel stiff, dry, or less flexible. That does not make protein “bad”; it means your hair may need a different balance. If your breakage pattern points to color, heat, styling, or repeated stress, bond repair may be the better starting point.


### **Do I need a conditioner or treatment if I use a strengthening shampoo?**


Often, yes—especially if your hair is damaged, tangles easily, or feels rough after washing. A strengthening shampoo can support the cleanse step, while a treatment such as N°.3PLUS gives you a more focused pre-shampoo repair step.\[1\] If you want the supported OLAPLEX system results for breakage, hydration, smoothness, detangling, and conditioning, keep the full Nº.3PLUS, Nº.4, and Nº.5 system together.\[2\]


Your next best move is simple: read your hair’s pattern, choose the strengthening approach that fits it, and build from there. Repair when repair is the job. Maintain when maintenance is the job. That is how a routine starts to feel less like trial and error—and more like confidence, wash after wash.
